gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the energy a named reviewer drew from the AC outlet the Anker SOLIX S2000 carries about 53 Wh per pound against about 44 for the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (labels: 56.3 vs 51.7), nor that the "10,000 cycles" the cited powerbencher page gives the Anker is Anker's figure to 60% capacity (6,000 to 80%, against Jackery's 4,000 to 70%).
standout_why: Compared against powerbencher.com (cited), slopsheets.com, powerstations.reviews, keptpowered.com, thiswatt.com, smartgadgetkit.com and offgridbenchmark.com; solargenreview.com and jackery.com returned HTTP 429. powerbencher has rated Wh/lb (56.3 S2000, 51.7 Jackery) but measured nothing ("~85% assumed"), lists the S2000 at 10,000 cycles with no end-of-life percentage and the Jackery's cycle life as not published, then multiplies cycles by capacity across brands. slopsheets has rated Wh/lb but no S2000 and no cycle life. powerstations.reviews puts S2000 6,000 to 80% beside Jackery 4,000 to 70% but does not put them on one line and uses a flat 0.85 allowance. smartgadgetkit carries OutdoorGearLab's 1,740 Wh for the Jackery but never mentions the S2000. None pairs Notebookcheck's S2000 draw with a Jackery measurement, and none gives lb per continuous kW.
decides: It confirms the S2000 as lightest and widens its lead: 3.8 lb lighter on the makers' weights, and about 160 Wh more at the outlet on reviewers' figures despite a label 32 Wh smaller (different reviewers and loads, so indicative). The table footnote is that no row delivers 2,000 Wh at the outlet: about 1,900 (S2000), 1,740 (Jackery 2000 v2), 1,600-1,850 (C2000 Gen 2). The same normalising shows the cost: per continuous watt the S2000 is the heaviest of the three (23.8 lb/kW vs 18.0 and 17.4), so the Jackery 2000 v2 is the lightest that runs a load above 1,500 W. One caution for the pick rule: Anker's US store today says S2000 orders placed on or after Nov 26 ship in 7-13 weeks, while Jackery's store says the 2000 v2 ships by Dec 11. Under the four-week rule the S2000 may have to be listed as lightest but not be the pick, unless another seller we link has stock.

findings.label: Maker's capacity, weight, output

findings.note: Rated Wh per lb = 2,010 / 35.7 = 56.3. The page names no boost or lifting mode. Default AC input capped at 1,150 W (full in 2.3 h); up to 1,600 W with UltraFast Mode in the app.

findings.label: Price and ship time, Anker US store
findings.value: $649.99 (shown as $350 off $999.99); orders placed on or after Nov. 26 ship within 7-13 weeks
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S2000 Portable Power Station (Anker SOLIX US)

findings.label: Cycle life, both points Anker publishes
findings.value: 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity; 10,000 cycles to 60% capacity
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX S2000 Portable Power Station (Anker SOLIX US)
findings.note: The 10,000 figure powerbencher quotes without a percentage is the 60% one. Our arithmetic: a straight line between Anker's two points gives about 8,000 cycles at 70%, Jackery's line; Anker publishes no 70% figure, so label it as interpolation.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, Notebookcheck
findings.value: just over 1,900 Wh at a continuous AC load of about 250 W (about 95% of rated)
findings.source_title: 2 kilowatt hours have never been this light: Anker Solix S2000 power station review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2026-10-07)
findings.note: Measured usable Wh per lb = 1,900 / 35.7 = 53.2; lb per delivered kWh = 18.8. Also from the review: 16.2 kg, "the lightest 2-kWh power station we have come across so far"; bypass mode 2,300 W; about 3 W bypass consumption; a little over 10% of charge per 24 h with AC left on; 6,000 cycles to 80%.

findings.label: Maker's capacity, weight, output, price, ship date
findings.value: 2,042 Wh LiFePO4; about 39.5 lb (17.9 kg); 2,200 W continuous / 4,400 W surge; switchover under 20 ms; 0-100% in about 1.7 h; $999.00 (compare-at $1,899.00); pre-order, ships by Dec. 11
findings.source_title: Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 Portable Power Station (Jackery US store record)

findings.label: Usable AC energy and weight, OutdoorGearLab

findings.label: Efficiency, idle draw and measured peak, The Solar Lab

findings.label: Cycle life basis
findings.source_title: Jackery 2000: every generation compared, and which to buy (powerstations.reviews)
